kind.title: Tracker
kind.description: Where tickets come from. Prep Cook reads tickets, posts updates and takes plan decisions through this tracker.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: The account Prep Cook uses to read and write tickets.

email.label: Email
email.helper: The account email the API token belongs to.

apiToken.label: API token
apiToken.helper: Stored locally and used to authenticate with the tracker.

botIdentity.label: Agent account id
botIdentity.placeholder: Leave blank to use the token's account
botIdentity.helper: The account the agent's own tracker comments are recognised by. Blank uses the account the API token belongs to.

import.title: Import
import.description: Defaults used when previewing tickets to import.

projectKey.label: Project key
projectKey.helper: The tracker project tickets are imported from and filed into.

importFilter.label: Import filter
importFilter.placeholder: e.g. sprint in openSprints() AND assignee = currentUser()
importFilter.helper: Optional query (JQL for Jira) applied when previewing tickets to import. {project_key} is substituted.

watcher.title: Ticket pickup
watcher.description: Polls the tracker for newly created high-priority bugs and imports them straight into Plan, assigned to you, so the orchestrator starts the RCA immediately. Meant for an always-on machine.
watcher.enabledHelper: Only tickets created while the watcher is running (24h lookback) are picked up; already-imported keys are skipped.
watcher.projectHelper: The board that receives the imported tickets.
watcher.pickupHelper: Which new tickets to pick up. {project_key} is substituted; a created-recently window is added automatically. Leave empty for the default P0/P1 bug filter.
watcher.assignedHelper: Tickets assigned to the orchestrator's tracker account start automatically, whatever their priority: new keys import straight into Plan, already-imported tickets sitting in To Do advance to Plan. Watches the updated timestamp, so assigning an existing ticket works. Empty disables it globally; only boards with pickup enabled are polled. Leave the status out of this filter — the watcher decides on status itself. Suggested: project = {project_key} AND assignee = currentUser()
watcher.pollHelper: How often the tracker is checked for new tickets.
watcher.boardsHint: Defaults for the board selected here. Other boards are watched with their own filter — see Board overrides under Orchestrator.

workflow.title: Workflow
workflow.description: How the board's stages show on the ticket, which statuses mean the work shipped, and which priorities are blockers.
workflow.statusHelper: The tracker status a ticket moves to when Prep Cook starts each stage. Blank leaves the ticket where it is (Planning falls back to In Progress).
workflow.shippedHelper: Comma-separated status names that mean the work shipped. Comments on these tickets go to triage, and a ticket that leaves them can file a follow-up.
workflow.blockerHelper: Comma-separated priorities whose merge requests are labelled Blocker and announced in Slack.

approvers.title: Plan approvers
approvers.description: Who may approve, request changes on or re-plan a plan from a tracker comment.
approvers.label: Approvers
approvers.helper: Import the people who can be assigned tickets in this project, then tick the ones allowed to decide. Nobody ticked means nobody can decide from the tracker. The orchestrator's own account is never eligible, so it cannot sign off its own analysis.
approvers.error: Could not load users from the tracker. Check the connection settings above.
approvers.empty: No one imported yet — import from the tracker to choose approvers.

section.title: Stage Playbooks
section.description: Prompt templates used when launching an agent for a workflow stage, keyed by "{work class}:{stage}". Planning playbooks open with the target repository's slash commands and must record a planning verdict on the issue before it can move to Executing.

entry.helper: Supports the placeholders jira_key, title, description, and spec_path, written inside double curly braces; they are substituted when the agent is launched.
entry.usingGlobal: Inheriting the global text — editing here overrides it for this board only.

scope.label: Editing
scope.helper: Pick a board to override individual stage playbooks for that repo only.

pool.title: Worktree Pool
pool.description: Reuse warm worktrees (with dependencies and build caches intact) across tasks instead of creating a fresh temp worktree per workspace. Requires the treehouse CLI on this machine; changes take effect after a restart.

enabled.label: Enable worktree pool
enabled.helper: When treehouse is missing or the pool is full, workspaces silently fall back to regular temp worktrees.

maxTrees.label: Max worktrees per repository
maxTrees.helper: Upper bound on pooled worktrees kept per repository (1-9). Each slot holds a full checkout plus its build caches on disk; slot numbers drive per-stack port offsets (slot × 10) and offset 90 is the highest the dev stack tooling accepts, so 9 is the ceiling.

root.label: Pool root directory
root.helper: Optional. Directory holding the pools; treehouse stores them under <root>/.treehouse. Leave empty for the default.

save.success: Worktree pool settings saved. Restart the app to apply them.
save.error: Failed to save worktree pool settings.

general.title: Stage Orchestrator
general.description: Background automation that watches the kanban board and acts on tickets assigned to you: launches planning/execution/review agents, creates MRs, and runs clean-up. Changes apply on the next poll — no restart needed.

mode.label: Enable automatic agent launches
mode.helper: When off, nothing runs automatically; stage playbooks can still be started manually from the issue panel.

pollInterval.label: Poll interval (seconds)
pollInterval.helper: How often the board is scanned for eligible tickets.

deployedRetention.label: Auto clean-up after (days in Deployed)
deployedRetention.helper: Tickets sitting in Deployed longer than this move to Clean-up automatically (archiving workspaces and closing the Jira ticket). Leave empty to disable.

cleanupRetention.label: Delete after (days in Clean-up)
cleanupRetention.helper: Tickets sitting in Clean-up longer than this are deleted from the board. The MR, the Jira ticket and any RCA in the knowledge base all survive; only the card and its comments go. Tickets with a pinned workspace or a human takeover are never deleted. Leave empty to keep cards forever.

autonomy.label: Autonomy mode (drive tickets through the gates)
autonomy.helper: High-confidence plans self-approve and advance; finished implementations move to Review; reviewer verdicts are acted on (approve → Push MR, request-changes → fix loop). Low confidence escalates to Slack. MRs stay drafts — a human always merges. Meant for the always-on teammate runner.

autonomyIterations.label: Review-fix rounds before escalating
autonomyIterations.helper: How many request-changes → fix → re-review cycles autonomy runs before pinging Slack and leaving the ticket for a human.

investigationThreshold.label: Investigation threshold (RCAs per pattern)
investigationThreshold.helper: When an RCA-graph node accumulates this many linked root-cause analyses, a P2 [Investigation] Jira story is created and imported into To Do. Re-fires after the same number of new RCAs land on the node.

hostSharing.title: Host sharing
hostSharing.description: Lets teammates open this machine's workspaces through the relay — the gesture for an agent runner, so anyone can inspect the agent's sessions from their own app.
hostSharing.label: Share this machine's workspaces with my organization
hostSharing.helper: Applies immediately on save (the relay must be enabled and this machine signed in). Turning it off makes the host private again.

approvals.title: Plan approvals
approvals.description: How a planning agent puts its spec or RCA in front of a person. Whatever is chosen here, a decision can also be made from the card, the tracker ticket or the approvals API.
approvals.lavishHelper: The document carries Approve and Request changes buttons and opens in a Lavish review session. Off: the document has no buttons, and the agent waits for a decision from the card, the ticket or the API.

slack.title: Slack notifications
slack.description: Best-effort notifications for events that need a human: low-confidence RCA escalations, autonomy review-loop caps, and repeated launch failures.
slack.webhookHelper: A Slack incoming-webhook URL (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…). Leave empty to disable.
slack.botTokenHelper: A Slack bot token (xoxb-…). When set together with a channel, planning escalations post via the Slack API so teammate replies in the escalation thread are fed back to the blocked agent. Requires chat:write and channels:history (or groups:history) scopes, and the bot must be in the channel. Leave empty to post via the webhook only (no reply polling).
slack.channelHelper: The channel escalations post to when a bot token is set, e.g. C0123456.

projects.title: Automated projects
projects.description: Only tickets in these projects are automated. Pick which local repositories agent workspaces check out for each project.
projects.empty: No projects configured yet — add one below.
projects.reposHelper: Local repositories checked out for auto-launched agent workspaces. At least one is required.
projects.noRepos: No local repositories found. Add one under Settings → Repositories first.
projects.addHelper: Remote kanban projects from your organizations.
projects.boardHint: Connect a board to list projects
projects.notFound: This board no longer exists on the remote, so the orchestrator can't scan it — remove the entry.

save.success: Orchestrator settings saved. They apply on the next poll.

maxLaunchesPerTick.label: Max launches per tick
maxLaunchesPerTick.helper: New agent launches allowed per scan (P0s first). Keeps a backlog from bursting the Claude seat when a pause lifts.

board.overridesHelper: Anything left on Inherit — or blank — uses the global setting above. Record only what differs for this board.
board.labelHelper: Short name tagged onto this board's RCAs as board:<label>, so one export can be split per repo.
board.watcherHelper: Poll the tracker for this board's tickets and import them into Plan.
board.jqlHelper: Selects this board's tickets; {project_key} is substituted. Boards sharing a tracker project separate here — by component, label, or module.
board.assignedJqlHelper: This board's assigned-pickup filter; blank inherits the global one (there is no per-board off — scope the filter instead). Requires ticket pickup on this board. Boards sharing a tracker project add their routing here (component, label) just like the pickup filter above.
board.trackerKeyHelper: Only when this board's tickets live in a different tracker project. Site and credentials stay global.
board.slackHelper: Set to Off to silence this board without clearing the global webhook.
board.autoAssignHelper: Assign the humans who last touched the changed lines as MR reviewers.
board.reviewerMapHelper: One email=login (GitHub or GitLab username) per line, added to the global map (entries here win).
board.excludeHelper: One email per line, added to the global exclusions.
board.botLoginsHelper: One GitHub or GitLab login per line, added to the global bot list.
board.deployWatchJobHelper: The CI job (GitLab) or Actions workflow (GitHub) whose success means a merged change is live on staging. Leave blank to turn the staging watch off for this board.
board.deployWatchRefHelper: The branch that job deploys from. Both fields are needed for the watch to run.
board.autonomyHelper: Run this board's stages unattended; Inherit follows the global setting.
board.retentionHelper: Days in Deployed before the ticket moves to Clean-up.
board.cleanupRetentionHelper: Days in Clean-up before the card is deleted (the MR, Jira ticket, and kb records survive).
board.playbooksHint: Playbook text for this board is edited under Settings → Playbooks.

workspaceRetention.label: Workspace retention (days)
workspaceRetention.helper: Delete finished workspace records — and their sessions, logs and turns — this many days after their worktree was cleaned up. Pinned workspaces are never removed. Blank keeps everything for ever.

status.title: Claude seat
status.description: The runner signs Claude Code in with a subscription seat (an OAuth login, not an API key). If it expires or the account signs in elsewhere, every agent launch fails until it's re-authenticated here.
status.healthyHelper: The last probe succeeded. Agents can run. With the seat monitor on (orchestrator.seat_monitor in the config file), the seat is re-checked automatically every few hours.
status.degradedHelper: The last probe failed to authenticate. Agents are paused until someone re-runs the login on the runner (below), then re-checks.

recheck.error: Couldn't re-check the seat. Try again in a moment.

reauth.title: Re-authenticate the seat
reauth.description: Re-auth is an interactive browser login that has to run on the runner, so it can't be done from this screen. Run the command on the box, then use Re-check now to confirm.
reauth.commandHelper: Opens Claude Code's login flow inside the container. Sign in as the agent's Claude account and paste the code it prints.
reauth.step1: SSH (or SSM) onto the runner and run the command above.
reauth.step2: Complete the browser sign-in as the agent's Claude account, then paste the authorization code back into the prompt.
reauth.step3: Return here and click Re-check now — the status should flip to healthy.

defaultTargetBranch.label: Default Target Branch
defaultTargetBranch.helper: The default base branch for new workspaces. Worktrees branch off from this branch and PRs will target it.

scripts.description: Read from .prepcook/scripts.toml at the repository root. Prep Cook never edits that file: change the scripts there and reload.
scripts.loadError: Could not read the scripts manifest.
scripts.hint: Prep Cook installs, builds, starts, seeds and tests a repository with the commands in .prepcook/scripts.toml at its root, and only [app] start is required. docs/scripts.md describes every key, the environment the scripts receive and a full example. A minimal file:

secrets.title: Required secrets
secrets.missingHint: Add the missing values in Settings → Secrets; a stand-up stops with secret-missing until they are set.

run.title: Test run: {{step}}
run.reportUnavailable: The run's report is no longer available.

save.confirmSwitch: You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to switch repositories? Your changes will be lost.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.description: Values the repository scripts need that must not be committed. Every script receives each one as $NAME and $PREPCOOK_SECRET_NAME, and Prep Cook redacts the values from logs, comments and messages. Values are never shown here.
secrets.loadError: Failed to load the secrets store.

file.label: Secrets file
file.helper: NAME=VALUE lines, written with mode 0600. PREPCOOK_SECRETS_FILE points Prep Cook at a different file, and an environment variable PREPCOOK_SECRET_<NAME> overrides the file's entry.

add.title: Add a secret
add.description: Saving a name that already exists replaces its value.

name.label: Name
name.helper: Letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit.
name.invalid: Use letters, digits and underscores, and do not start with a digit.

value.label: Value
value.helper: Sent once and never displayed again.

remove.dialogDescription: Scripts that require this secret stop with secret-missing until it is set again.

required.title: Required by repositories
required.description: Names listed in a repository's [secrets] requires that have no value yet.
required.allSet: Every secret the repositories require has a value.

enrollmentCode.loginRequired: Log in to generate a pairing code.

remoteProjects.noProjects: No projects yet. Create one to get started.

defaultRepos.noBranches: No branches found for this repository

boardRequired.title: No board

sentry.title: Sentry
sentry.description: Optional. Exposes the Sentry MCP server to agents so they can inspect issues, errors, and events while investigating. It is installed only while an access token is set here, in the environment (SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN), or as a Prep Cook secret of that name.
sentry.tokenHelper: Sentry user auth token (scopes: org:read, project:read, event:write). Overrides SENTRY_ACCESS_TOKEN from the environment when set; takes effect on save.
sentry.hostHelper: Hostname of a self-hosted Sentry instance. Leave blank for Sentry SaaS (sentry.io).

reviewers.title: Merge request reviewers
reviewers.description: Blame-based reviewer picks and review-comment watching for orchestrator-created merge requests on GitHub and GitLab.
reviewers.autoAssignHelper: On new merge requests, blame the changed lines at the target branch and request review from the top human author who is mapped below.
reviewers.mapHelper: One email=login per line, the login being the person's GitHub or GitLab username. Blame candidates not listed here are named in a comment instead of assigned.
reviewers.excludeHelper: Never pick these as reviewers (bot and shared identities are excluded automatically).
reviewers.botsHelper: Logins whose review comments are never fed back to the agent (GitLab token bots containing “_bot” and GitHub apps ending in “[bot]” are ignored automatically).

connectors.title: Agent connectors
connectors.description: The MCP servers loaded into every agent session, probed live via `claude mcp list` on this host. Every listed server's tool schemas cost context tokens in every session — keep this list lean.
connectors.unavailable: Could not run the probe — the claude binary is missing or errored.
connectors.fixHelper: Fixing auth is manual by design: for remote MCP servers run `claude` interactively on the runner and use /mcp to complete OAuth; claude.ai account connectors are managed at claude.ai signed in as the agent account. First-party tools (Jira attachments, Slack threads) need no extra auth.

usage.empty: No usage recorded in this window yet.
